name: ABS / Stability Control
description: Factory four-channel ABS with StabiliTrak/ESC and Performance Traction Management: an Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM) mounted to the Brake Pressure Modulator Valve (BPMV). Race options: keep the factory unit (requires factory CAN/ECM/steering-angle environment), install a stand-alone Bosch Motorsport ABS kit, or delete ABS entirely with a dual-master bias bar.

components.name: Brake Pressure Modulator Valve (BPMV) + EBCM (factory ABS/ESC unit)
components.description: Hydraulic modulator with inlet/outlet solenoid valves and return pump, plus the bolted-on EBCM that runs ABS, traction control, StabiliTrak and electronic brake-force distribution (no separate proportioning valve on Gen 6). Two inlets from the tandem master, four outlets (LF, RF, LR, RR). It needs CAN data (ECM torque, steering angle, yaw/lat-g, wheel speeds) — with a stand-alone race ECU and factory harness removed it will not function.
components.location: Engine compartment, driver side forward area near the frame rail (exact Gen 6 position not confirmed in sources – placed approximately).

factory.name: GM EBCM/BPMV, four-channel ABS with StabiliTrak (Gen 6 Camaro)
factory.notes: Product guide: "Four-wheel disc with four-channel ABS". Requires GM scan tool (GDS2/Tech2-type) automated bleed after the BPMV is opened.

raceOptions.name: Bosch Motorsport ABS M5 / M7 kit

hardware.item: Brake pipe fitting to BPMV inlet
Brake pipe fitting to BPMV outlet
hardware.spec: Metric ISO bubble-flare tube nut (M10x1 typ.)

hardware.notes: GM table: "Electronic brake control module bolt" 3 N·m. Quantity typical for Bosch-style EBCM.

hardware.item: Brake pressure modulator valve nut (BPMV to isolator/bracket)
hardware.notes: GM table value is 3 N·m (light – rubber isolators).

installNotes: Install bracket, then BPMV on isolators; connect inlet pipes first, outlet pipes second (do not cross LF/RF/LR/RR).
Bleed conventionally, then run the scan-tool ABS automated bleed to purge the secondary circuits.
Only retain if the build keeps the factory body/chassis electronics and CAN; otherwise choose Bosch M5/M7 or delete.
inspection: Check for DTCs after each event if retained.

components.name: Bosch Motorsport ABS M5 / M7 kit (race alternative)
components.description: Stand-alone motorsport ABS: hydraulic unit with integrated ECU, its own wheel-speed inputs, yaw/accel sensor, and a driver map switch (typically 12 settings) that trades stopping distance for stability. Used in GT4/TCR/Trans Am-type cars; designed to work with dual race masters and is independent of the factory CAN. M7 is the newer generation with more channels of configuration.
components.location: Typically in the passenger footwell (cool, protected) or engine bay on vibration mounts; hydraulic unit level, ports accessible. Placed here in passenger footwell x≈0.86, z≈-0.35.

raceOptions.name: Bosch Motorsport ABS M5 Kit
raceOptions.notes: Kit = hydraulic unit/ECU, wiring, yaw-rate sensor, switch; calibration by Bosch-trained dealer per car.

hardware.item: Hydraulic unit port adaptors (M10x1 / M12x1 to -3 AN)
hardware.spec: Steel adaptor with sealing (cone/bubble or washer per Bosch port)
hardware.torque: M12x1 ≈ 18–20 N·m; M10x1 ≈ 14–16 N·m (typical metric brake fittings)
hardware.notes: Confirm port type and values in Bosch kit manual.

installNotes: Mount, plumb with -3 AN, wire to PDM switched power and to sensors; have the kit calibrated (vehicle weight, wheelbase, tire rolling radius, bias).
Bleed with the unit's bleed routine/pump cycle per dealer instructions.
inspection: Download fault memory after each event.
Check wheel-speed sensor air gaps and wiring for damage after off-track excursions.

components.name: Front wheel speed sensors
components.description: Active (Hall/magneto-resistive) sensors that read the magnetic encoder ring built into the front hub bearing seal. Feed the EBCM (or the race ABS / data logger).
components.location: Pressed into the front hub bearing / knuckle at each front corner.

factory.name: GM active wheel speed sensor (integral with/plugged into front hub bearing on Alpha platform)
factory.notes: Bearing encoder is the "tone ring"; keep magnetic debris off it.

raceOptions.name: Retain OEM sensors with Bosch M5/M7 (Bosch kit supports active sensors)
raceOptions.notes: Saves fabrication; verify compatibility with your Bosch calibrator.

hardware.item: Wheel speed sensor harness clips/bracket bolt
hardware.notes: Sensor retention spec not found in sources; small M6 GM brackets are typically 9–10 N·m.

installNotes: Install with the hub bearing; route harness along the flex brake hose/strut with clips so it cannot contact the tire at full lock and bump.
inspection: Check harness for heat/abrasion damage near the caliper and brake duct.

modelRef.dimensions: ~35 mm sensor at the back of the hub bearing

components.name: Rear wheel speed sensors
components.description: Active wheel-speed sensors at the rear hub bearings (encoder in bearing).
components.location: Rear knuckle / hub bearing each side.
installNotes: Route harness away from halfshaft boots and exhaust.

modelRef.dimensions: ~35 mm sensor at the back of the rear hub bearing

components.name: Yaw-rate / acceleration sensor
components.description: Inertial sensor needed by stability control (factory) or by Bosch race ABS for corner-braking logic. Must be mounted rigidly near the car's center of gravity, aligned to the car axes.
components.location: Tunnel / floor near CG, x≈1.6, y≈0.25, z≈0.

factory.name: GM inertial sensor (integrated in another module on Gen 6 – verify)

raceOptions.name: Bosch Motorsport yaw-rate sensor (supplied with ABS kit)

specs.Orientation: Arrow/axis aligned to vehicle X forward as marked

installNotes: Mount on a stiff bracket, not on flexible sheet metal.

modelRef.features: Sensor module with connector and 2 mounting feet

components.name: ABS delete (front tee / rear distribution block)
components.description: When ABS is deleted, each race master feeds its axle directly: the front master to a tee/distribution block that splits to LF and RF, and the rear master to a tee at the rear crossmember. Many sanctioning bodies (NASA/SCCA prod-based classes) allow ABS removal; check your class rules.
components.location: Front tee on the firewall/footbox; rear tee on rear subframe area (x≈2.55).

raceOptions.name: -3 AN billet tee / 3-way distribution block
raceOptions.notes: Choose one with a bleed or sensor port.

hardware.torque: ≈ 110–130 in-lb (12–15 N·m) for steel -3 AN on 37° flare; ≈ 75–95 in-lb (8.5–11 N·m) for aluminum fittings

installNotes: Mount blocks at the highest practical point or provide a bleed port to avoid trapped air.
